messages.subject: 2  conditionalPanels, when one is open the other is closed?
parts:
Forgive me for my newbie question, but I'm trying to make 2 conditional panels in a way that when one is open the other is closed. 

My first unsuccessful attempt where I did not insert the logic to switch the status, just trying to get the initial status and show only the corresponding panel.

library(shiny)

shinyUI(fluidPage(
  
  title = "Diamonds Explorer",
  
  #checkboxInput("smooth", "Smooth"),
  
  conditionalPanel(
    condition = "cond == 0",
    plotOutput('plot'))   ,
  
  hr(), 
  conditionalPanel(condition = "cond != 0",
                   tabsetPanel(
                     tabPanel("H", p("H")),
                     tabPanel("M", p("M")),
                     tabPanel("I", p("I")),
                     tabPanel("R", p("R"))
                   )),
  hr()
))

library(shiny)

cond <- 1

shinyServer(function(input, output) 
  {

  output$plot <- renderPlot({
    
    hist(runif(1000))
    
    
  })
})

messages.subject: Re: 2  conditionalPanels, when one is open the other is closed?
parts:
First, I would have an actionButton records your desire to switch panels:

actionButton(inputId = "action", label = "Something Else Please")

Then, my first attempt was to call a reactiveValues() inside a conditionalPanel, but that failed. So instead I used the trick of looking for odd/even numbers of actionButton clicks, i.e.

condition = "input.action % 2 == 0"

See the code and runGist below.

This did not work, WHY?

In server.R
    values <- reactiveValues(cond = 0)
    observe({ 
      if(is.null(input$action) || input$action == 0){return()} 
      values$cond <- isolate(1-values$cond) # switch between 0 and 1
    }) 

In ui.R, the conditionalPanel:
condition = "value.cond == 0"

library("shiny")
runGist("https://gist.github.com/anonymous/8273912")

See the code:
https://gist.github.com/anonymous/8273912

messages.subject: Re: 2 conditionalPanels, when one is open the other is closed?
parts:
João, the solution David offered should work, except I'd change one thing:

output$cond <- reactive({
   ... return something, probably TRUE/FALSE ...
})
outputOptions(output, "cond", suspendWhenHidden=FALSE)

With the bolded command, you do not need the textOutput("cond") in ui.R. But you can refer to output.cond in the conditionalPanel conditions.

Patrick, "value.cond == 0" didn't work for you because "values" is just a reactiveValues variable that you happened to declare in your server.R code--there's nothing special about it that would cause it to automatically be available in the browser side, which is where the conditionalPanel conditions are evaluated. There *is* something special about the input and output variables; both sides know these values. Does that make sense?
